original_text: The central value of its measured energy was $2.46\times 10^{20}$ eV.
injected_text: The central value of its measured energy was $2.57\times 10^{20}$ eV.
rationale: The Telescope Array paper (TelescopeArray:2023sbd) reports the Amaterasu particle energy as 2.44×10^20 eV with an uncertainty of roughly 0.11×10^20 eV (∼5%), so shifting the quoted central value from 2.46 to 2.57 (a change of +0.11×10^20 eV ≈ 1σ) places the mis-quote just outside the 1σ envelope while remaining within 2σ — realising a C·S1·type-2 qualifier mis-quote with the cite key left intact.
ground_truth_description: The quoted central energy of the Amaterasu event was changed from 2.46×10^20 eV (close to the published 2.44×10^20 eV) to 2.57×10^20 eV, a shift of approximately 1σ outside the reported uncertainty.

We use this fact to argue that  at least some of these these cosmic rays are relatively light magnetic monopoles and

injected_text:
We use this fact to argue that  at least some of these these cosmic rays are relatively light magnetic monopoles, but

rationale: [2026-05-01 patch: original_text re-anchored from `10$^{20}$` to `10$^{02}$` because numerics.S2.t1 already perturbed that magnitude in the abstract; the general-module flip stacks on top.]  The abstract now claims the MM fraction above 10^20 eV is consistent with zero and unconstrained, directly contradicting the body (Section IV, Table 1) which reports positive f_MM values reaching 0.520 at 100–110 EeV with Z_MM values hinting at tension, and the conclusion which explicitly states a substantial MM fraction may be coming from the local void — a major internal contradiction detectable by cross-checking abstract against results.
ground_truth_description: The abstract's claim about the MM fraction above 10^20 eV was flipped from 'can be found from full sky observations' to 'is consistent with zero and cannot be meaningfully constrained', contradicting Table 1 and the Discussion section which report non-zero f_MM values and positive Z_MM trends.
